question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -11 \\ 17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
question.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set $\{v,w\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-3)\cdot 3+(-11)\cdot (-4)+17\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-3)\cdot 5+(-11)\cdot 4+17\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -12 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
